fg.title: Fear & Greed Index
fg.subtitle: Market sentiment from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed) — from breadth, volatility and bond/credit signals.
fg.no_data: Not enough data available to compute the index for {index}.
fg.macro_note: Note: breadth is computed locally for the selected index; the macro components (VIX, bonds, credit) are US/global and serve as a risk backdrop. If a series (e.g. VIX3M) is not fully up to date, the index uses the latest available value.
fg.methodology_md:
The **Fear & Greed Index** condenses seven market signals into a single value from **0 (extreme fear)** to **100 (extreme greed)**. It measures not price direction but the *sentiment* behind it — whether the market is driven by fear or complacency.

**Breadth** (across all index members, from the simulation database):

- **Momentum** — the index above/below its SMA125, normalised against its own history.
- **Breadth** — average of % of members above SMA200, % with RSI > 50 and the bullish share (Markov regime).
- **52-week strength** — share of members near their 52-week high.

**Volatility & hedging** (macro series):

- **Volatility** — VIX relative to its 1-year range (high VIX = fear).
- **Term structure** — VIX vs. VIX3M; when the curve tips into backwardation, fear rises. Substitutes the classic put/call ratio, which is not available from the data source.
- **Safe haven** — 20-day return of the index minus TLT (Treasuries): when stocks beat bonds, greed prevails.
- **Junk-bond demand** — 20-day return of HYG (high yield) minus LQD (investment grade): tight spreads = risk appetite.

**Normalisation:** each component is mapped to 0–100 (breadth directly as a percentage, the macro series via z-score or percentile of their own history) and then averaged with equal weights.

**Sources:** price/volume data and indicators from the local database (`asset_simulation`, `yf_*`); macro series VIX, VIX3M, TLT, HYG, LQD from the active data provider. The index is a **sentiment gauge, not a buy/sell signal**.

banner.title: Silvesto, your portal for growth.
banner.strategy_how: The system applies a **quantitative multi-strategy approach** with {n_strategies} configured {strategy_word} across {n_indices} indices simultaneously.
banner.strategy_step1: 📡 **Daily scan** — Every trading day all assets in the tracked indices are ranked by their Sortino ratio, trend score and technical indicators.
banner.strategy_step2: 🟢 **Automated buy** — The top *N* ranked assets per index are bought as soon as the configured buy condition is met (e.g. overallValueTrend ≥ 60, Heikin-Ashi bullish, MACD above signal).
banner.strategy_step3: 🔴 **Rule-based sell** — Each position is sold as soon as the sell condition triggers (e.g. RSI crosses below its EMA or the trend score drops), independent of the other positions.
banner.strategy_step4: ⚖️ **Risk management** — Take-profit and stop-loss levels are pre-calculated from ATR data. The Markov regime filter avoids buying into bear-market phases.
banner.strategy_advantage: **Key advantage:** fully systematic, no emotional bias, runs 24/7 via the built-in scheduler — human intervention is only needed to review results or adjust strategy parameters.
banner.strategy_analysis_caption: Key figures per strategy — realised gain counts closed trades only, potential gain marks open positions at their last price.
banner.bh_caption: Each strategy versus a buy-and-hold blend of the indices it trades (same window, full budget invested throughout). Shows whether the strategy beats the index — and how much capital it ties up on average to do so.
banner.bh_legend: Avg. capital deployed = average capital tied up ÷ budget (lower = less exposure). Return on capital = gain ÷ capital actually deployed (real. = closed only, pot. = incl. open positions). Edge = gain minus buy & hold.
banner.hint_global_tensions: ⚠️ **Note on current global tensions:** Due to heightened geopolitical uncertainty, signals from the **Value Trend Strategy** should be treated as **informational hints only** and not as a direct trading recommendation. Please form your own judgement before acting.

corr.methodology_title: ℹ️ Methodology — what is measured here
corr.methodology_body:
- **Measure:** Pearson correlation of **daily log returns** (ln(C_t / C_t-1)), *not* of price levels or price trends. External tools/AI that instead compare price or trend paths can arrive at different values — up to the opposite sign (e.g. BTC/Gold: returns slightly positive, price trends can diverge).
- **Window:** rolling **30** or **90 trading days**. Shorter windows react faster and tend to run "hotter" than long ones for risk assets — compare magnitudes only within the same window.
- **Range:** −1 (perfect opposite) … 0 (decoupled) … +1 (perfect co-movement). Classification: |r|≥0.6 strong, ≥0.3 moderate, ≥0.15 weak, otherwise practically decoupled.
- **Instruments:** S&P 500 `^SPX`, Bitcoin `BTC-EUR` (proxy for BTC-USD — return correlation practically identical), Gold `GC=F`, US Dollar Index **`DX-Y.NYB`**, Copper `HG=F`, US Treasuries 10Y `ZN=F`.
- **Data:** local daily prices from the app database; recomputed daily by the scheduler. Other tools with a different data provider/snapshot or period will differ accordingly.
- **History:** the dollar index, copper and treasuries are only available locally from ~2024, so their curves start later.
corr.interp_no_history: Too little overlapping history to draw a conclusion.
corr.interp_rising: The correlation **{dir}** (Δ {delta} vs. ~1 month) — the coupling is strengthening.
corr.interp_falling: The correlation **{dir}** (Δ {delta} vs. ~1 month) — the coupling is loosening.
corr.pair.spx_btc.label: S&P 500 ↔ Bitcoin
corr.pair.btc_gold.label: Bitcoin ↔ Gold
corr.pair.spx_usd.label: S&P 500 ↔ US Dollar Index
corr.pair.copper_spx.label: Copper ↔ S&P 500
corr.pair.zn_spx.label: US Treasuries (10Y) ↔ S&P 500
corr.pair.spx_btc.narr_pos: Bitcoin moves in lockstep with US equities — it behaves like a high-beta risk asset (a tech proxy) and offers little diversification in this regime.
corr.pair.spx_btc.narr_neg: Bitcoin is decoupling from equities and following its own driver — its diversification value in a portfolio rises.
corr.pair.spx_btc.context: Historically unstable: often clearly positive during risk-off phases since 2020, closer to zero in calm periods.
corr.pair.btc_gold.narr_pos: Bitcoin and gold move together — both are traded as a store of value / hedge against currency debasement (the 'digital gold' thesis holds up).
corr.pair.btc_gold.narr_neg: Bitcoin and gold diverge — the 'digital gold' thesis does not hold right now; the two react to different drivers.
corr.pair.btc_gold.context: Usually weak: both are seen as an inflation/debasement hedge but react with different sensitivity to real yields and risk appetite.
corr.pair.spx_usd.narr_pos: Equities and the dollar rise together — unusual; often points to US-specific strength or capital inflows into US assets. It can also signal stress when the dollar rises as a safe haven.
corr.pair.spx_usd.narr_neg: Normal state: a stronger dollar weighs on US equities (pricier exports, tighter financial conditions) — the inverse coupling is intact.
corr.pair.spx_usd.context: Typically negative. A sign flip into positive territory is a warning signal (regime change / risk-off).
corr.pair.copper_spx.narr_pos: Copper ('Dr. Copper') and equities in lockstep — a consistent growth / risk-on signal; the growth outlook supports both.
corr.pair.copper_spx.narr_neg: Copper and equities diverge — the equity rally is not confirmed by the real economy (possible growth doubts).
corr.pair.copper_spx.context: Usually positive: copper is regarded as a leading indicator of the global economy; a falling correlation can foreshadow a growth slowdown.
corr.pair.zn_spx.narr_pos: Bonds (ZN) and equities rise together — both benefit from falling rates / easier monetary policy. Conversely they fall together when rate fears dominate (an inflation / rate-shock regime).
corr.pair.zn_spx.narr_neg: Classic diversification regime: bonds rise when equities fall (flight to safety) — the 60/40 portfolio works.
corr.pair.zn_spx.context: A negative sign is the 'healthy' diversification case; a turn into positive (the 2022 pattern) hits balanced portfolios hard.
